items.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023
items.q: And in one of the chapters of that book it was the story of Miles Davis came to Dizzy Gillespie asking him for help...

ctx.x: You just answered one of the questions I had written down, so thank you. Does the fact that you play piano impact your trumpet improvising?

Big time, and a great question. That was, after I listened to that, later on I got in my hands one of those jazz history books. And in one of the chapters of that book it was the story of Miles Davis came to Dizzy Gillespie asking him for help to get into the more deeper concept of improvisation and knowledge of the changes and all those things. And Dizzy said, “Okay I can help you. Let’s go to the piano.” And Miles said, “Piano? What?” Dizzy said, “Okay, that’s the only way I can explain it to you.” When I read…

really made that thing into my brain and I said you know what? I have to get familiar with the piano. And I never regret it. By the way, I spend a lot more time with the piano than with the trumpet. Because the piano for composition, for arranging, for creating, for understanding the chord sequencing and the basis, not only the basis but only all the variation and a tentative chord that you can find, and the piano has something else that is you can hear the thing but you can see. You understand what I mean? With…
